feedback: No race evidence exists yet, so this is a baseline, not a diagnosis. I built the controller with weights proportional to sensor x-position, which needed no compensation for the sensor layout. The 10 mm pitch under a 12 mm footprint gives overlap across the 25 mm tape, so at least two sensors should read tape through moderate bends. The main risk I see is the sensor lead. At 5 cm ahead of the axle, the controller reacts late at speed, which may cause oscillation. Your own intent flags this, so I agree it is worth testing. Hold the current geometry for this race. Once the telemetry returns, use steering_oscillation to decide on a shorter lead, and line_loss_events with max_error to decide on a wider spread. If neither shows a problem, keep the geometry and tune only the controller.
requested_changes: Hold the baseline geometry for the next race. The first telemetry is the only evidence for any change.
If steering_oscillation is high at speed, try moving the sensors forward to about 6 to 7 cm ahead of the axle (y about 0.06 to 0.07), keeping the spread the same.
If line_loss_events or max_error is high in tight bends, try widening the sensor spread to about ±0.03 m (x = -0.03 to +0.03) while keeping the sensor count at five.
